messages.content: "Can you help me calculate the energy required for a phase change? I have a science experiment where I am first melting 500 grams of ice at 0 degrees Celsius, then I am freezing it back. After that, I am vaporizing the same mass of water at 100 degrees Celsius and then condensing it back to liquid state. The substance I am using for this experiment is water. Can you tell me how much energy is required or released during each of these phase changes?"

function.name: thermo_calculate_energy
function.description: Calculate the energy required or released during a phase change using mass, the phase transition temperature and the specific latent heat. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

mass.description: Mass of the substance in grams.

substance.description: The substance which is undergoing phase change, default is 'water'

message.content:
Below is a quick “energy budget” for your experiment.  
All values assume **pure water** and standard ambient pressure (≈ 101 kPa).

| Step | Process | Temperature | Latent Heat (per gram) | Energy Change |
|------|---------|-------------|------------------------|---------------|
| 1 | Ice → Liquid Water (Melting) | 0 °C | \(L_{\text{fusion}} \approx 334\;\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}}\) | +\(mL_{\text{fus}}\) |
| 2 | Liquid Water → Ice (Freezing) | 0 °C | \(L_{\text{fusion}}\) | –\(mL_{\text{fus}}\) |
| 3 | Liquid Water → Steam (Vaporisation) | 100 °C | \(L_{\text{vapour}} \approx 2260\;\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}}\) | +\(mL_{\text{vap}}\) |
| 4 | Steam → Liquid Water (Condensation) | 100 °C | \(L_{\text{vapour}}\) | –\(mL_{\text{vap}}\) |

With \(m = 500~\text{g}\):

---

### 1️⃣ Melt 500 g of ice  

\[
Q_{1}=m\,L_{\text{fus}}
=500~\text{g}\times 334~\frac{\text{J}}{\text{g}}
=166{,}700~\text{J}
\simeq 167~\text{kJ}
\]

*(Positive sign means energy absorbed from surroundings.)*

---

### 2️⃣ Freeze 500 g of water  

Same magnitude as above but released:

\[
Q_{2}=-166{,}700~\text{J}\ (\approx -167~\text{kJ})
\]

---

### 3️⃣ Vaporise 500 g of water  

\[
Q_{3}=m\,L_{\text{vap}}
=500~\text{g}\times 2260~\frac{\text{J}}{\text{g}}
=1{,}130{,}000~\text{J}
\simeq 1{,}130~\text{kJ}
\]

---

### 4️⃣ Condense 500 g of steam  

\[
Q_{4}=-1{,}130{,}000~\text{J}\ (\approx -1{,}130~\text{kJ})
\]

---

#### Net effect

If you perform all four steps consecutively on the same sample,

\[
Q_{\text{total}} = Q_1+Q_2+Q_3+Q_4 = 0
\]

so no net energy is stored or removed—just transferred between phases.

> **Quick reference:**  
> • Melting/Freezing ≈ ± 167 kJ for 500 g  
> • Vapourising/Condensing ≈ ± 1 130 kJ for 500 g

Feel free to plug these numbers into your lab notebook or simulation!
